newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy cuts discount rate to 6.75 percent.
newsitem.headline: Italy cuts discount rate to 6.75 percent.

text.p: The Bank of Italy said Tuesday it would cut the official discount rate to 6.75 percent from 7.50 percent, as inflation was steady.
The cut will take effect on Wednesday, a Bank of Italy statement said. The previous change in the discount rate was on Oct.23, when it was reduced from 8.25 percent.
The Bank's Lombard rate was simultaneously cut to 8.25 percent from a previous 9.00 percent.
A bank statement said inflation had remained at moderate levels over the past few months, in line with objectives set for the current year.
Preliminary data from Italian cities released earlier Tuesday showed that inflation for January was expected to remain steady at 2.6 percent, according to analysts.
